blocks.text: Tsawwassen Foreclosures & Court-Ordered Sales — Frequently Asked Questions

parts.t: How do court-ordered foreclosure sales work in Tsawwassen?

When a mortgage lender obtains an Order for Conduct of Sale from the BC Supreme Court, the Tsawwassen property is marketed on the MLS®. After an initial offer is accepted and conditions are satisfied, the sale goes to a court hearing where a judge or associate judge approves the final transfer.
Do Tsawwassen court sales include both freehold and leasehold homes?
Yes. A Tsawwassen foreclosure can be a municipal freehold property in

What does the Schedule A addendum mean for Tsawwassen foreclosure buyers?

Schedule A is required on every BC court-ordered sale. It states that the seller makes no representations or warranties regarding the property's condition, permits, or appliances, and that the buyer accepts the home strictly "as-is, where-is."
How do sealed bids work at a BC Supreme Court approval hearing?

If competing buyers show up at the court hearing, all competing offers must be unconditional, accompanied by a certified deposit, and submitted in sealed envelopes before 9:45 a.m. under Practice Direction 66. The court typically approves the highest net unconditional offer.
What due diligence is essential before submitting an unconditional court bid?

Complete a professional home inspection, review the title search and charges (including geotechnical covenants in English Bluff or flood covenants in Beach Grove), confirm financing and appraisal approval with your lender, and review all strata records before removing subjects.
Why does the Tsawwassen foreclosure page sometimes show zero active listings?
Court-ordered sales in Tsawwassen are infrequent because most distressed owners sell consensually before the court grants conduct of sale.
